verdict.reasoning: Patient states, "it's lasting for like three days" referring to diarrhea.

Transcript confirms frequent diarrhea disrupting activities ("I can't go to work because I need to go," "I just go into the toilet every 10 minutes") and no blood ("No, I haven't noticed any blood"). However, it never specifies that the diarrhea is watery, so describing it as "watery" is added information.

Patient reports, "the pain is mainly focused in the center area of the abdomen, like under the belly button and sometimes I can hear my stomach, like the cramps," which is consistent with central crampy abdominal pain.

Patient says they ate fruit (strawberries) for breakfast and later vomited once: "I had some fruit... Then I got a bit of nausea and I vomited... that was it," and clarifies the red content was strawberries, not blood.
When asked about chest pain, patient replies, "No, I haven't. I haven't noticed any chest pain."
Patient reports chronic breathing problems from asthma: "I always have problems with my breathing because of the asthma," so they do not deny shortness of breath.
Patient says, "I didn't have any fever recently... I don't think so. I don't think. I don't know, maybe," overall indicating denial of clear fever.
In response to past medical problems, patient states, "I have asthma and I take some inhaler."
Patient says, "I take an inhaler" and later, "my inhaler kind of run out... I have this brand, but I bought a new one here," indicating current inhaler use and a new brand.
Patient reports, "my father... he died about 10 years ago of cancer."

Patient notes staying home due to toilet needs: "I don't walk very far because I need to go to the toilet now and then, so I'm spending some time at home," consistent with preferring to stay home due to frequent toilet use.
When asked about pressing on tummy, patient replies, "Oh, it does a little bit," indicating slight tenderness on palpation.
Doctor states, "this is normally called gastroenteritis, so an infection over the tummy," identifying the assessment as gastroenteritis.

Doctor attributes symptoms to eating something bad: "you might have eaten something bad and it's causing your tummy pain... normally called gastroenteritis," and diarrhea is non-bloody ("No, I haven't noticed any blood") with vomiting once after food, fitting likely dietary gastroenteritis with non-bloody diarrhea and vomiting.

Patient notes baseline asthma symptoms but no new issues: "I always have problems with my breathing because of the asthma... a part of the normal. I haven't, I haven't," indicating no acute exacerbation and usual control with inhaler.
Doctor advises, "Number one is to drink lots of water and fluids because you're losing lots at the moment."
Doctor advises, "Number two is to make sure and look out for any fevers. So if you start getting a temperature..." which is monitoring for fever.
Doctor recommends, "Three is stay home for the time being until you get slightly better."
Doctor states, "Normally things like antibiotics don't help. They make the situation worse," effectively advising to avoid antibiotics.
Doctor advises escalation: "If you feel you're getting much worse, then I would suggest you go and see your GP in real life in person."
